results.instruction: Fill the portafilter with pre-ground coffee.
Distribute the coffee evenly over the filter.
Tamp the coffee down using a tamper until it is firm and flat.
Insert the portafilter handle into the espresso machine.
Start the espresso extraction immediately.
Stop the extraction when the espresso reaches 25 to 30 milliliters.
Listen to the suggestion of making an Americano.
Listen to the instruction to use hot water just off the boil.
Listen to the instruction to avoid boiling water in the cup.
Listen to the instruction to add espresso to the hot water to dilute it.
Listen to the announcement that the next steps are making a cappuccino and latte.
Press the steam button down on the espresso machine.
Wait for the steam light to go out and then come back on to change the boiler temperature.
Place the metal milk jug into the milk frothing device.
Position the tip of the steam wand underneath the surface of the milk.
Turn on the steam and feel the bottom of the jug as it heats up.
Stop steaming once the milk reaches the desired temperature.
Observe the foam on top of the milk, noting it is about a third foam.
Lower the milk jug to the cup and begin pouring with a wiggle motion.
Continue pouring to create a rich foam layer for the cappuccino.
Listen to the explanation of the cappuccino's name origin.
Listen to the explanation of the latte meaning milk in the town.
Listen to the mention of cafe latte or latte macchiato.
Pick up a stainless steel milk pitcher containing frothed milk.
Pour the liquidy, rich textured milk from the pitcher into the cup to create a latte.
Observe the finished cafe latte with its layered appearance in the white cup.
View the split-screen comparison showing the latte, espresso shots, and other coffee preparations.
